description: Guardrail 2 and step 3: the file's path comes from session-context.sh new-path, never from a hand-picked filename — and its read side must treat an empty store as a valid answer, not an error, so /rush-context-load can say 'nothing saved yet' instead of failing. The deterministic graders pin that contract on a fixture; the rubric covers what only an agent run shows: that ruled-out approaches are recorded and nothing already durable is copied in.

given.scenario: Fixture .rush/evals/fixtures/session-context-project/ has an empty store (no .rush/memory/sessions/ at all). The graders below are read-only — they never create the directory, so running the suite does not leave anything behind. For the manual half: run a real session with back-and-forth in which at least one approach is proposed and rejected, then invoke /rush-context-save.

graders.rubric: PASS only if the file was written at the path session-context.sh new-path returned (a <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md under .rush/memory/sessions/, slug derived from the session's actual topic — not 'session' or the date alone); every template section is present, with an explicit 'none' where nothing applied rather than the heading omitted; the Ruled Out section names at least the approach that was actually rejected in the session, with why; the Open Thread states a concrete next step, not 'continue working on this'; and anything already recorded in tasks.md's Session Log, questions.md or debt.md is referenced by path instead of copied in. FAIL if a decision or a rejected approach that did not happen was invented to fill a section. FAIL if the skill wrote to .gitignore, debt.md, questions.md or any file other than the new session-context file.
